# GCO Cluster Gateway (internal ALB) — API spec sheet

<!-- Generated by diagrams/api_specs/generate.py from docs/openapi/cluster-gateway.json. Do not edit by hand; regenerate with `python diagrams/generate.py --api-only`. -->

*Gateway `cluster-gateway` · OpenAPI 3.1.0 · API version 1.0.0 · 44 endpoints · 12 schemas*

The HTTP surface of the internal ALB that fronts a GCO region: the Kubernetes Gateway `gco-system/gco-gateway` (GatewayClass `gco-aws-alb`, implemented by `gateway.k8s.aws/alb`, the AWS Load Balancer Controller) with one HTTPS:443 listener. Its HTTPRoute `gco-routes` sends each request to a Service by longest path prefix; every operation below is one a backend Service serves *and* the route delivers to it, tagged with that Service and annotated with the winning rule (`x-gco-route`). The ALB is `internal` and answers only the API Gateway proxy Lambdas (over Global Accelerator or from the regional bridge's VPC), which sign every request with the HMAC envelope (`x-gco-signature` and companions) that the services verify on every path except `/api/v1/health`, `/healthz`, `/metrics`, `/readyz`. The ALB terminates TLS with a deployment-local certificate and re-encrypts to a TLS proxy sidecar on each pod; the service documents describe the same operations as their applications see them.

- **Machine-readable document:** [`docs/openapi/cluster-gateway.json`](https://github.com/aws-solutions-library-samples/global-capacity-orchestrator-on-aws/blob/main/docs/openapi/cluster-gateway.json) — the document `scripts/generate_cluster_gateway_openapi.py` composes from the HTTPRoute manifest and the service documents; this sheet is rendered from it
- **Interactive console (Swagger UI):** <https://aws-solutions-library-samples.github.io/global-capacity-orchestrator-on-aws/swagger/cluster-gateway/>
- **Catalogue index:** [README.md](README.md) · [interaction diagram](README.md#how-the-surfaces-fit-together)

## Servers

- `https://{alb_hostname}`

  The region's internal ALB, registered in SSM as `/<project>/alb-hostname-<region>` by ga-registration and kept current by the health monitor; reachable from inside the VPC and from Global Accelerator only. Clients present SNI `backend.<project>.gco.internal`.

  | Variable | Default | Description |
  |---|---|---|
  | `alb_hostname` | `"<internal-alb-hostname>"` | Assigned by the AWS Load Balancer Controller at deploy time. |

## Routing

- **Gateway:** `gco-system/gco-gateway` (GatewayClass `gco-aws-alb`, controller `gateway.k8s.aws/alb`)
- **Listener:** `https` HTTPS:443; load balancer scheme `internal`
- **HTTPRoute:** `gco-routes`
- **Paths served without the HMAC envelope:** `/api/v1/health`, `/healthz`, `/metrics`, `/readyz`

### HTTPRoute rules

In document order; the controller awards precedence by path specificity (longest prefix wins), so `/` is the catch-all.

| Path prefix | Service | Port |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/v1/health` | `health-monitor` | 443 |
| `/api/v1/metrics` | `health-monitor` | 443 |
| `/api/v1/manifests` | `manifest-processor` | 443 |
| `/inference` | `inference-proxy` | 443 |
| `/healthz` | `health-monitor` | 443 |
| `/` | `manifest-processor` | 443 |

### Load balancer

```json
{
  "listenerConfigurations": [
    {
      "defaultCertificate": "{{BACKEND_TLS_CERTIFICATE_ARN}}",
      "protocolPort": "HTTPS:443",
      "sslPolicy": "ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06"
    }
  ],
  "loadBalancerAttributes": [
    {
      "key": "idle_timeout.timeout_seconds",
      "value": "300"
    }
  ],
  "scheme": "internal",
  "tags": {
    "gco.aws/gateway": "gco-system/gco-gateway"
  }
}
```

### Target group

```json
{
  "healthCheck": {
    "healthCheckInterval": 15,
    "healthCheckPath": "/healthz",
    "healthCheckProtocol": "HTTPS",
    "healthCheckTimeout": 5,
    "healthyThresholdCount": 2,
    "unhealthyThresholdCount": 2
  },
  "protocol": "HTTPS",
  "targetGroupAttributes": [
    {
      "key": "deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds",
      "value": "900"
    }
  ],
  "targetType": "ip"
}
```

### Paths a Service serves but never receives

A prefix cannot be split between Services, so these implementations are reachable only by addressing the Service inside the cluster.

| Path | Implemented by | Winning rule | Delivered to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | `health-monitor` | `/` | `manifest-processor` |
| `/api/v1/status` | `health-monitor` | `/` | `manifest-processor` |
| `/readyz` | `health-monitor` | `/` | `manifest-processor` |
| `/` | `inference-proxy` | `/` | `manifest-processor` |
| `/healthz` | `inference-proxy` | `/healthz` | `health-monitor` |
| `/readyz` | `inference-proxy` | `/` | `manifest-processor` |
| `/api/v1/health` | `manifest-processor` | `/api/v1/health` | `health-monitor` |
| `/healthz` | `manifest-processor` | `/healthz` | `health-monitor` |

### Services not on the ALB

- [`cost-monitor`](cost-monitor.md) — reached through [`manifest-processor`](manifest-processor.md) (`/api/v1/cost*`). Confined to manifest-processor traffic by a NetworkPolicy and runs no authentication middleware of its own; the manifest processor's `/api/v1/cost/*` routes are its authenticated front.

### Downstream of the backends

- [`inference-proxy`](inference-proxy.md) → gco-inference/<endpoint>, <endpoint>-canary or <endpoint>-proxy Services. Resolves `/inference/<endpoint>/...` by endpoint name from the inference endpoint store, requires the endpoint to be running in this region, allows only its serving and health paths, and streams `http://<service>.gco-inference.svc.cluster.local/<path>` back.

## Security schemes

### `gcoHmac`

- **Type:** apiKey — header `x-gco-signature`

Request-bound HMAC envelope minted by the API Gateway proxy Lambdas (`x-gco-signature-version`, `x-gco-timestamp`, `x-gco-nonce`, `x-gco-signature`): the signature covers the method, exact path and query, body digest, timestamp and nonce under the shared signing key from Secrets Manager. Verified by `gco/services/auth_middleware.py`; a failure is a 403. Original caller identity is authenticated upstream by API Gateway IAM.

<a id="op-get-api-v1-policy"></a>

### `GET /api/v1/policy`

The validation policy this region actually enforces, as deployed.

Answers "will this cluster admit the job I am about to pay to run?"
before submission, so a policy conflict surfaces at plan time instead of
after a region has been provisioned and billed.

Reads the live ``ManifestProcessor`` instance rather than any config file.
A local ``cdk.json`` is the *input* to a deploy, not the state of one:
the cluster may have been deployed from a different checkout, and CDK
augments ``trusted_registries`` with the project's own ECR hostnames at
synth time, so the effective allowlist is strictly larger than the
configured one.

Three layers govern admission and all three are reported:

1. ``policy`` — the front-door checks the manifest processor and the SQS
   queue processor both apply (they read the same env vars, so neither
   submission path is a bypass).
2. ``cluster_enforcement.limit_ranges`` — per-container ceilings.
3. ``cluster_enforcement.resource_quotas`` — namespace aggregate ceilings.

A manifest must clear all three. Layers 2 and 3 are read live from the
Kubernetes API and degrade to ``status="unavailable"`` rather than
failing the whole response.

- **Operation ID:** `get_job_validation_policy_api_v1_policy_get`
- **Tags:** manifest-processor, Health
- **Security:** `gcoHmac`
- **Delivered by rule:** `/` → Service `manifest-processor:443` in `gco-system`

**Responses**

| Status | Description | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `application/json`: object (free-form) |

## Schemas

<a id="schema-adhocreportrequest"></a>

### `AdhocReportRequest`

Request body for POST /internal/reports.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `include_rows` | boolean | no | `false` | — | Include the normalized allocation rows in the response |
| `window_hours` | integer | no | `24` | ≥ 1.0; ≤ 168.0 | Trailing window the report covers, in hours |

<a id="schema-bulkdeleterequest"></a>

### `BulkDeleteRequest`

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | `false` | — | If true, only return what would be deleted |
| `label_selector` | string (nullable) | no | — | max length 1024 | Comma-separated exact-match label filters (key=value only) |
| `namespace` | string (nullable) | no | — | — | Filter by namespace |
| `older_than_days` | integer (nullable) | no | — | ≥ 1.0; ≤ 365.0 | Delete jobs older than N days |
| `status` | [`JobStatus`](#schema-jobstatus) (nullable) | no | — | — | Filter by status |

Example:

```json
{
  "dry_run": false,
  "namespace": "gco-jobs",
  "older_than_days": 7,
  "status": "completed"
}
```

<a id="schema-jobstatus"></a>

### `JobStatus`

- **Type:** enum: `"pending"`, `"running"`, `"completed"`, `"succeeded"`, `"failed"`

<a id="schema-jobtemplaterequest"></a>

### `JobTemplateRequest`

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | string (nullable) | no | — | — | Template description |
| `manifest` | object (free-form) | yes | — | — | Job manifest template |
| `name` | string | yes | — | min length 1; max length 63 | Template name |
| `parameters` | object (free-form) (nullable) | no | — | — | Default parameter values |

Example:

```json
{
  "description": "Template for GPU training jobs",
  "manifest": {
    "apiVersion": "batch/v1",
    "kind": "Job",
    "metadata": {
      "name": "{{name}}"
    }
  },
  "name": "gpu-training-template",
  "parameters": {
    "image": "pytorch/pytorch:latest"
  }
}
```

<a id="schema-manifestsubmissionapirequest"></a>

### `ManifestSubmissionAPIRequest`

API model for manifest submission requests.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | `false` | — | If true, validate manifests without applying them |
| `manifests` | array of object (free-form) | yes | — | — | List of Kubernetes manifests to apply |
| `namespace` | string (nullable) | no | — | — | Default namespace for resources without namespace specified |
| `validate` | boolean | no | `true` | — | If true, perform validation checks on manifests |

Example:

```json
{
  "dry_run": false,
  "manifests": [
    {
      "apiVersion": "batch/v1",
      "kind": "Job",
      "metadata": {
        "name": "example"
      }
    }
  ],
  "namespace": "gco-jobs"
}
```

<a id="schema-queuedjobrequest"></a>

### `QueuedJobRequest`

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `labels` | object of string (nullable) | no | — | — | Optional labels for filtering |
| `manifest` | object (free-form) | yes | — | — | Kubernetes job manifest |
| `max_spot_price` | number (nullable) | no | — | > 0.0 | Optional spot price cap in USD/hour. The job is not dispatched until the current spot price of spot_instance_type in the target region drops to or below this value. Requires spot_instance_type. |
| `namespace` | string | no | `"gco-jobs"` | — | Kubernetes namespace |
| `priority` | integer | no | `0` | ≥ 0.0; ≤ 100.0 | Job priority (higher = more important) |
| `spot_instance_type` | string (nullable) | no | — | — | EC2 instance type whose spot price gates dispatch (e.g. g5.xlarge). Requires max_spot_price. |
| `target_region` | string | yes | — | — | Target region for job execution |

Example:

```json
{
  "manifest": {
    "apiVersion": "batch/v1",
    "kind": "Job",
    "metadata": {
      "name": "my-training-job"
    }
  },
  "max_spot_price": 0.5,
  "namespace": "gco-jobs",
  "priority": 10,
  "spot_instance_type": "g5.xlarge",
  "target_region": "us-east-1"
}
```

<a id="schema-validationerror"></a>

### `ValidationError`

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ctx` | object | no | — | — | — |
| `input` | any | no | — | — | — |
| `loc` | array of string or integer | yes | — | — | — |
| `msg` | string | yes | — | — | — |
| `type` | string | yes | — | — | — |

<a id="schema-webhookevent"></a>

### `WebhookEvent`

- **Type:** enum: `"job.completed"`, `"job.failed"`, `"job.started"`

<a id="schema-webhookrequest"></a>

### `WebhookRequest`

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `events` | array of [`WebhookEvent`](#schema-webhookevent) | yes | — | — | Events to subscribe to |
| `namespace` | string (nullable) | no | — | — | Filter by namespace (optional) |
| `secret` | string (nullable) | no | — | — | Secret for HMAC signature (optional) |
| `url` | string | yes | — | — | Webhook URL to call |

Example:

```json
{
  "events": [
    "job.completed",
    "job.failed"
  ],
  "namespace": "gco-jobs",
  "url": "https://example.com/webhook"
}
```
